newsitem.title: UK: Chase confirms Bosnia reaches debt deal.
newsitem.headline: Chase confirms Bosnia reaches debt deal.

text.p: Bosnia and Herzegovina reached an agreement in principle late Monday with commercial bank creditors to restructure its share of debt assumed under the 1988 new financing agreement (NFA) with the former Yugoslavia, Chase Manhattan Bank said in a statement.

Although the exact amount was not disclosed, a Western official told Reuters in Sarajevo late Monday that Bosnia would service $404 million, of which a portion would not be repaid until the country achieved specific growth targets.

Chase said completion of the transaction, which is expected by December 31, would constitute a "fundamental step" for Bosnia and Herzegovina to achieve its goal of normalising relations with the financial community and the international markets.

Chase, which acted as chair of the International Coordinating Committee for the London Club of commercial bank creditors, also said Bosnia and Herzegovina would be released from any joint and several obligations under the NFA.
Last June, the London Club issued a one year waiver which required Bosnia to forge an agreement by midnight on Monday.
If the deadline had expired without a deal, Yugoslovia would have been allowed to enter the negotiations.
Under the terms of the agreement, Chase said Bosnia and Herzegovina would issue bonds denominated in deutschemarks to eligible creditors which would be exchanged for a portion of the NFA principal.
The bonds, expected to be listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange, would be issued in exchange for 10.58 percent of the NFA principal and for similar amounts under related agreements.
As part of the restructuring, the bonds would have a basic amount of principal equal to 37.5 percent of the NFA debt and a performance amount equal to 62.5 percent.
Chase said the basic amount would be amortized in stepped-up payments over 13 years following a seven-year grace period.

It said the interest rate would be set at the London Interbank offered rate (LIBOR) plus 13/16 of one percent but Bosnia and Herzegovina would pay a fixed rate of two percent in the first four years, three percent over the next three years and 3.5 percent during the following three years.

The principal amount of the bonds would be increased by the performance amount that would be effective on the interest payment date following the World Bank's determination Bosnia and Herzegovina achieved GDP per capita of at least $2,800.
Chase said the GDP target would be indexed to Germany's consumer price index from 1997 for two consecutive calendar years beginning with the seventh year after issuance and ending with the 20th year.
In addition, interest on the performance amount would accrue from the date it is added to the principal amount on the bonds and would be payable at the same rates as applicable to the basic amount.
The performance amount would be amortized in equal payments over 12 years following the addition to the bonds.
